targetText:
The analysis of landed property in its various historical forms is beyond
the scope of this work. We shall be concerned with it only in so far as a
portion of the surplus-value produced by capital falls to the share of the
landowner.
explanation: Ground rent is the share of surplus value that flows to landowners simply because they hold legal monopoly over land. The capitalist farmer extracts surplus value from workers, then surrenders part of it to the landowner as rent.
summary: Ground rent is the portion of surplus value that falls to the landowner due to monopoly ownership of the soil.
